agenda_items.title: Chair's Verbal Update
agenda_items.minutes:
Ādisōke Update
Chair Luloff reported productive progress on Ādisōke construction in October, with continued work on the stunning red cedar exterior, roof, and stone base. Interior activities include painting, electrical, tile and custom millwork are all ongoing. In closing, he encouraged everyone to follow the project online.
Osgoode Branch 100th Anniversary
Chair Luloff invited everyone to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Osgoode branch on November 22, and highlighted events planned that day, including a puppet show, remarks at 11:30am, local history displays, a magician, and crafts.
Canadian Library Month Wrap-Up
Chair Luloff thanked trustees, staff, clients, and community members for celebrating Canadian Library Month in October. He highlighted four musical performances that drew 507 attendees and fostered in-person community connections. Client testimonials reflected appreciation for OPL’s welcoming spaces and diverse offerings. Social media engagement reached over 40,000 people, with more than 12,000 views. In the branches, 3,981 new library cards were issued. He concluded by affirming that while Library Month has ended, OPL remains open and welcoming to all year-round.
Recent passing of former OPL Board Trustee
Chair Luloff expressed sadness over the recent passing of former OPL Board member Phil Rocco, who served from 2004 to 2006. He praised Phil’s legacy as an educator, mentor, and community leader, noting his lasting impact on many lives. On behalf of the Board, he extended sincere condolences to Phil’s family and friends.
MOTION OPL 20251104/1
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chair’s verbal update for information.
Results: Received

agenda_items.title: Chief Librarian / Chief Executive Officer's Report
agenda_items.minutes:
Ottawa’s Children’s Storytelling Festival
Sonia Bebbington, Chief Librarian and CEO, shared that OPL recently partnered with the Ottawa Storytellers and the Odawa Native Friendship Centre to host the Children’s Storytime Festival. The event captivated children with oral storytelling, and Ms. Bebbington highlighted the role in developing literacy, creativity, and emotional connection, complemented by print literacy and storytelling. Approximately 210 participants attended. Ms. Bebbington thanked all involved in making the festival a success.
Treaties Recognition Week, International Inuit Day and Métis Day
Ms. Bebbington shared OPL’s activities for Treaties Recognition Week, including a reading list and an author event with Armand Garnet Ruffo on November 6. She also highlighted OPL’s first year participating in International Inuit Day on November 7, featuring National Film Board (NFB) film screenings at select branches. Additionally, OPL will observe Métis Day on November 16 with more NFB screenings and colouring sheets by Métis artist Emily Frost, highlighting Michif language in partnership with the Assembly of Seven Generations.
Financial Literacy Month
Ms. Bebbington shared upcoming Library programming for Financial Literacy Month (FLM), including sessions for seniors, tweens, teens, and parents. A session with author Shannon Lee Simmons on November 13 will focus on tweens, teens, and parents, and a “Food and Finance” workshop on November 26 will focus on meal planning. OPL also supported City-led initiatives in priority neighbourhoods with financial literacy bookmarks for FLM. She emphasized OPL’s broad range of resources available to support financial literacy for all ages.
Upcoming Closures
Ms. Bebbington noted that all OPL locations will be closed November 11 to observe Remembrance Day, and on November 20 for the OPL Employee Forum. She noted that the forum is an important opportunity for employees to get together, share ideas, and discuss initiatives, and appreciate and recognize the hard work of their colleagues. She encouraged everyone to take some time on these days to visit the OPL website and explore the wealth of OPL’s digital collections and resources, from magazines to movies and music and more!
MOTION OPL 20251104/2
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the Chief Librarian/CEO’s report for information.
Results: Received

sub_agendas_items.title: Early Literacy Services at OPL
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Sarah Macintyre, Division Manager, Client Services and Myra Skaronski, Division Manager, Branch Services provided a presentation (held on file with the Chief Librarian/Chief Executive Officer) on the topic of early literacy services at OPL. The following is a summary of the information presented:
In response to a question from Vice-Chair Fisher regarding how early literacy programming has evolved over the last five years, Ms. Macintyre underlined the core tenets (based on the American Library Associations’ research-based Every Child Ready to Read toolkit) remain the same, and that recent changes have related more to pandemic and post-pandemic service challenges, including increased virtual options for programming. She further referred to the Program Strategy as the framework to ensure OPL continues to deliver on its clearly-articulated service commitments. Ms. Bebbington noted additional recent commitments to increase French children’s programming, in response to client needs both among Francophone families and those with children in French immersion programs. Ms. Skaronski further noted an increased commitment in recent years to inclusive early literacy programming, for example the sensory storytime pilot.
The Chair thanked staff for the presentation and the hard work that goes into early literacy services at OPL.
There being no further questions, the presentation was RECEIVED as presented.
MOTION OPL 20251104/3
That the Ottawa Public Library Board receive the presentation for information.
Results: Received

sub_agendas_items.title: 2026 Draft Operating and Capital Budget Estimates and Four-Year Capital Forecast

attachments.attachment_title: 2026 Draft Operating and Capital Budget Estmates and Four-Year Capital Forecast.pdf
Document 1 - OPL 2026 Draft Operating and Capital Budget Book.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Sonia Bebbington, Chief Librarian and CEO provided opening remarks, after which Anna Basile, Deputy CEO and Division Manager, Corporate Services, provided a PowerPoint presentation for Board members with an overview of the 2026 Draft Budget, including context, directions, efficiencies, operating requirements (regular operations and Central branch operations), capital allocations, user fees, Library Reserve, the four-year budget projection, recommendations and next steps. Matthew Pritz, Program Manager, Finance and Business Services and Diana Adjarska-Litzanova, City of Ottawa Financial Services were also available to respond to questions of clarification. A copy of the presentation is held on file with the Chief Librarian and CEO.
In summary, Ms. Bebbington noted the budget report outlines the Library’s full requirements for 2026; specifically, the operational requirements are differentiated in the budget as regular operations and Central branch specific operations. The amount dedicated to regular operations comes within the Council-directed budget allocation of $2.9M. Central branch specific operations are 20% funded within the same allocation.
Ms. Bebbington further noted that the proposed budget supports asset maintenance, includes a new branch for Old Hunt Club, enhances the client experience via increased collections funding and expanded Sunday hours, builds staff capacity for current services, and provides operating funds for the Central branch at Ādisōke. The budget reflects a prudent use of the Library Reserve to fund capital projects and strengthens financial stewardship through efficiencies and fair user fee updates. Staff welcome comments from the public and will continue to participate in councilor-led budget sessions, as requested, and staff will return to the board on December 2.
Following the presentation, staff responded to two questions of clarification from Board Members as follows:
Chair Luloff asked staff to confirm that the draft budget reflects OPL requirements, and Ms. Basile replied in the affirmative. The Chair further asked for confirmation that the strategy and mechanism for funding the priorities falling outside of the directed increase are for the City to propose. Ms. Basile confirmed in the affirmative: staff first recommend to the Board the use of funds within the Board’s control as per the tabled document. She continued that for the amounts above direction, City colleagues will speak to the strategies they intend to use when the City budget is tabled, noting that the budget book indicates a balanced bottom line.
Chair Luloff asked staff whether a representative from the City’s Finance Services team will be present at the December 2 meeting to respond to that question. Ms. Basile confirmed in the affirmative and further commented that staff are working closely with City colleagues.
Vice-Chair Fisher asked staff to confirm that capital initiatives being funded through the Library Reserve in 2026 ($2.945M) are one-time withdrawals. Ms. Basile confirmed in the affirmative, adding that she estimated the Library Reserve at $6.4M currently, which staff project may increase slightly based on the forecast for 2025.
Chair Luloff thanked the Finance and Business Services team as well as senior management for drafting a budget that meets the requirements for the next year, including the opening of the Central branch at Ādisōke, the largest cultural asset in which the City has invested. He was appreciative of the diligence of staff working with City colleagues to develop appropriate funding to ensure its success, while maintaining and growing the library system in alignment with plans and frameworks.
He noted staff are available to meet with Board members regarding the draft budget prior to the December 2 meeting.
There being no further discussion, the report was RECEIVED and TABLED as presented.
MOTION OPL 20251104/4
That the Ottawa Public Library Board:
Results: Received and tabled
Note: The report was tabled at the meeting. Documentation was posted publicly upon commencement of item.
